subject: Notice: throughput drop and p99 latency spike after model rollout
messages:
From: Sara Huang <sara@ledgerhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: LedgerHealth Engineering <support@ledgerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden p99 spike and throughput drop since this morning

Jordan —

We started seeing a pronounced latency spike across our critical text-generation path this morning (~05:30 PDT). p95 is up ~2.3x and p99 is up ~6x relative to yesterday, and throughput has dropped by roughly 28% on our 30s window. All calls are to the hosted endpoint using model variant v3b (A/B rollout: 40% traffic).

Steps we took on our side: restarted clients, switched to a fallback model id (v3a) — traffic to v3a appears to be fine. Attach a short sample of error logs and a trace. This is impacting our peak batch processing and customer-facing inference. Can we pause the rollout and revert the variant? We need an ETA for mitigation and whether Redwood will provide a credit for impacted SLA windows.

Attaching: customer_error_log_0922.json; trace_sample_v3b.txt

—Sara
VP Product, LedgerHealth

Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike and throughput drop since this morning

Sara — thanks for the quick heads up. I’m pausing the v3b portion of the rollout for your tenant now (reducing variant to 0%). Marcus and Avery are on this thread — Marcus, can you confirm the pause and start an initial triage?

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Huang <sara@ledgerhealth.com>, LedgerHealth Engineering <support@ledgerhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-22T08:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden p99 spike and throughput drop since this morning

Jordan / team — I confirm I've applied a hotfix to route LedgerHealth traffic off the v3b variant at 08:34 PDT (rollback to v3a). Repro/initial findings below:

- Symptom: elevated tail latency on v3b only; v3a remained within normal bounds.
- Immediate cause (hypothesis): v3b uses a larger KV cache window combined with a suboptimal attention kernel on the current serving instances; under the customer’s seq-length distribution this created intermittent serialization in the runtime’s KV eviction path, causing bursts of CPU work on the host and token emission stalls.
- Evidence: attached latency_histogram_qs.csv (p50/p95/p99 by minute), sample traces (trace_sample_v3b.txt) show repeated blocking in cache-evict() at ~30–40ms spikes. No quota throttles or infra OOMs observed.

Next steps I’ve kicked off:
1) Capture production flamegraphs for the 08:00–08:30 window (in progress).
2) Backport a kernel fallback to v3b that reduces the KV window and disables the new eviction heuristic; will test in a private canary and push if stable (ETA 3–4 hours).
3) Postmortem and regression ticket (JIRA-ISSUE-1284) opened.

Marcus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: latency_histogram_qs.csv (text/csv)]

Thanks for the fast action and rollback. Vivek (our infra lead) wants acknowledgement on two things: 1) whether this will recur if v3b is patched and reintroduced; 2) whether Redwood will consider a short-term credit for the impacted windows — this was user-facing.

—Sara

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Huang <sara@ledgerhealth.com>, LedgerHealth Engineering <support@ledgerhealth.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: technical mitigation plan and risk assessment

Team — quick update after the private canary run at 11:40 PDT: the kernel fallback eliminates the KV eviction stalls on the canary nodes and p99 for the canary traffic is back to baseline. However, performance delta vs v3a is still slightly higher for long sequences (~5–8% p95 overhead), so there is residual risk during full reintroduction.

Recommendation:
- Do a controlled, progressive reintroduction with observability gates: 5% → 20% → 50% for LedgerHealth only, watch p95/p99 and CPU. If any gate shows >10% p95 delta or >3x error-rate bump, abort.
- Offer LedgerHealth a rollback-window SLA credit for the affected 3-hour window (value TBD by finance/sales).

I’ve attached the traces and histogram used for the analysis. I’ll keep JIRA-ISSUE-1284 updated with flamegraphs and benchmark logs.

Marcus

Date: 2026-09-23T16:35:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood action plan & exec update — LedgerHealth incident 2026-09-22

Sara & Vivek —

Appreciate you raising this and for your patience while Marcus’ team investigated. Summary and next steps: 

Summary:
- Root cause: regression in v3b’s KV-eviction path combined with your workload’s sequence-length distribution, leading to intermittent token stalls and higher tail latency.
- Rollback status: v3b traffic for LedgerHealth was paused on 9/22 at ~08:34 PDT and remains off for your tenant.
- Impact window: 09:00–09:25 PDT 2026-09-22 (p99 and throughput deviation as described).

Action plan & offers:
1) Technical: We will follow Marcus’ progressive reintroduction plan with strict observability gates and a canary cohort limited to LedgerHealth initially. If anything diverges beyond the stated thresholds we will abort. Target: start progressive reintroduction tomorrow 09/24 09:00 PDT.
2) Compensation: I’ve flagged finance to draft a one-time service credit for the impacted window; Marcus’ notes and JIRA will be the audit trail. We’ll follow-up with a concrete credit proposal by EOD 09/24.
3) Communication: I’ll share the postmortem and the kernel fallback summary with your team once the investigation is complete (ETA 48 hours).

Internal action items: Marcus — continue the kernel-fallback work and validate on broad seq-length distributions; Avery — coordinate commercial credit and confirm finance contact; Rishi — FYI for exec visibility.

If you want us to keep v3b off permanently for LedgerHealth while we finish the root cause work, we can do that — let me know.

Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
